ranking.reader: Artem, a full-stack engineer who builds web products and LLM agents and writes about both. He wants items he can learn from or act on as a builder, not general tech news.

topics.description: Agent and automated pipelines and harnesses, LLM assistants, self-hosted/private AI platform development, and LLM/inference optimization.
exclude: AI policy, lawsuits, regulation, company drama, funding and business news
coding agents and their add-ons (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, plugins, skills) used while writing code (they belong to Tooling)
consumer AI apps with no engineering substance
include: building, running or evaluating LLM systems: agent harnesses, tool use, MCP, RAG, evals
inference and serving: self-hosted/local models, quantization, speed and cost
major model, API or dev-platform releases that change what or how you build
topics.name: AI Engineering

topics.description: Tools developers use to build software: editors, CLIs, libraries, and AI coding tools.
exclude: components for building LLM systems: agent frameworks, inference servers, evals (they belong to AI Engineering)
games, consumer apps, and utilities with no role in software development
nostalgia or legacy-systems threads, career and workplace discussion
include: tools used while building software: editors and IDEs, CLIs, terminals, debuggers, build tools, package managers, version control, databases
AI tools used while writing code: coding agents, editor plugins, Claude Code skills and hooks
new or notably improved open-source libraries and frameworks for building software
topics.name: Tooling

topics.description: Product and web trends, securities & market data, data visualization, browser performance, web architecture, and SEO.
exclude: general tech-company news, earnings and stock moves with no product angle
AI model releases (AI Engineering) and developer tools (Tooling)
games and demos that merely run in a browser
include: the web platform and browsers: new APIs, standards, rendering and browser performance
frontend engineering and web architecture: frameworks, CSS, performance, SEO
data visualization, and products built on market or financial data
product and web trends: notable launches and how web products make money
topics.name: Web Products

items.summary: PS5LM is a homebrew app that runs llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on a jailbroken PS5's RDNA 2 GPU and serves GGUF models over OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs to the local network. It now also runs decision models answering TypeSafe's /v1/systemone API.
items.title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console

items.summary: StarSkirmish Bench is a benchmark where each LLM gets one hour to write a StarCraft: Brood War Protoss bot in C++, then is scored by win rate against human-written and other LLM bots. v0.2 adds flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta run in their first-party CLI harnesses.
items.title: Show HN: Gemini 4 Argon plays StarCraft

items.summary: rStation is a shared research community where independent AI agents discuss research problems and publish reviewed papers, with humans welcome to observe. It organizes work around open problems such as the Riemann hypothesis and strongly regular graphs.
items.title: Show HN: rStation – A shared research lab for your AI agents

items.summary: Llmspeed is a tool that estimates how fast a local LLM will run on a given device before you buy hardware, using community benchmarks and projections derived from similar setups. It is open source on GitHub.
items.title: Show HN: Llmspeed – feel how fast a local LLM runs before you buy the hardware

items.summary: Once is a CLI tool that runs a command, prints stdout, and caches the result in a per-user background daemon, reusing it for the same command, directory, and tenant key until TTL expiry; a typical use is avoiding repeated 1Password fingerprint approvals.
items.title: Once: Cache CLI commands

items.summary: Diarea is a frontend leak scanner that finds exposed keys, source maps, API maps, debug globals, and private logic, then scores damage from Sealed to Gushing. It ships a CLI, Chrome extension, GitHub Action, and local read-only MCP server so coding agents can scan and fix leaks.
items.title: kriszwart/diarea

items.summary: Eido is an AI workspace for understanding code, building with an agent, and reviewing changes, keeping conversation and code together. Its 0.0.1 stable macOS release bundles pi 1.3.0 and adds OpenRouter model-list refresh, saved sharing preferences, and better tool restoration.
items.title: tony3liu/eido

items.summary: Stripe's announcement of three updates for fintechs: Global Payouts expanded to instant stablecoin payouts in 160 markets and traditional currency payouts in 100+, stablecoin card issuing via Stripe Issuing now in 27 EU countries (65+ worldwide), and unified APIs for global financial products.
items.title: New ways for fintechs to move money and expand globally

items.summary: Firefox 158 release notes, highlighting default JPEG XL image format support, Smart Window form filling suggestions, more accessible PDFs, a New Tab wallpaper library, and new translation languages.
items.title: Firefox 158 released with JPEG XL support by default

items.summary: A follow-along Ahrefs guide on automating content creation that explains how the author built a monthly Data Refresh Hub to automate repetitive updates to data-driven articles and how to apply the same process to other content tasks.
items.title: How to Automate Content Creation: A Follow-Along Guide

items.summary: Tracely-ai is trace-native CI/CD for AI agents: it grades production traces, clusters failures into issues, freezes bad runs into hermetic replayable regression cases and blocks the PR that would reship them. Tests come from real failing traces instead of hand-authored datasets.
items.title: jwuthri-cloud/Tracely-ai

items.summary: Hugging Face model page for deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, with setup snippets for Transformers, vLLM, SGLang and Docker serving. Only usage instructions are given; no capability details are stated.
items.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017

items.summary: OpenRouter listing for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, the Oct 17 2026 snapshot. It is described as a sparse MoE on DeepSeek's new Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture, activating 8B input/16B output from a 552B backbone, with native image understanding and compressed KV caching.
items.title: DeepSeek: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017

items.summary: rsi_eval is a lightweight Python SDK and CLI for evaluating recursive self-improvement methods across agent benchmarks: you keep your own improvement loop and call evaluate(), reusing pinned tasks, graders and a common result format across 24 bundled configurations.
items.title: Danielxu0208/rsi_eval

items.summary: ESP32sim is an MIT browser-based ESP32 firmware emulator that instruction-level emulates four ESP32 SoCs and boots the real mask ROM, bootloader, and unmodified application images via WebAssembly, with board support, GPIO/UART/timers, and virtual networking.
items.title: Show HN: Esp32sim – Run ESP32 firmware in the browser

items.summary: Sphinx is a free FOSS Git hook for agent-assisted development that pauses protected pushes and quizzes the developer on what the AI-written diff does when things go wrong, continuing only after a correct answer.
items.title: Show HN: Sphinx – A hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before shipping

items.summary: tsc-ts is an experimental TypeScript port of the TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler (tsgo), written in idiomatic TypeScript and compiled to native executables with scriptc; it ships npm packages and compares scanner/parser/binder output against tsgo.
items.title: Tsc-ts: TypeScript written in TypeScript

items.summary: An article explaining the removal of XSLT support in Chrome and Edge, and what will break versus what won't.
items.title: Chrome and Edge are removing XSLT: what breaks and what does not

items.summary: Ahrefs analysis of 66.6M free ChatGPT responses and 15M fan-out queries finds only 14.4% triggered web search, averaging about 1.6 queries when they did; 6.8% used site: and top searches skewed toward brand sites.
items.title: How ChatGPT Does Query Fan-Out (15 Million Queries Studied)

items.summary: A New York Times Magazine illustration by Nicholas Konrad visualizes a California ballot measure imposing a one-time 5% tax on billionaires’ net worth for 250 individuals, comparing the tax with their wealth, usual taxes, and opposition spending; transitioning circles convey the scale.
items.title: Scale of proposed billionaire wealth tax in California

items.summary: Russian-language GitHub guide for installing and running DeepSeek models locally on PC, Mac and server — covering Ollama, llama.cpp, API, RAG and agents. It is updated for October 2026, including DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and the 284B V4-Flash-0731 that fits in ~110 GB with llama.cpp.
items.title: justxor/deepseek-local-guide-ru

items.summary: DeepSeek API docs for the new Search and Fetch tools, which give agents and RAG apps live web content: Search returns structured results from DeepSeek's in-house engine, Fetch returns a page as Markdown. Both are raw JSON endpoints using the same bearer auth as the DeepSeek API.
items.title: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests

items.summary: arXiv paper presenting Hybrid Reasoning Agents, which switch between latent reasoning and text-based interaction in one generation process via a HybridLink module, with HybridSFT and HybridRL post-training. Reported gains: 10.4% better performance, 35.5–54.7% fewer tokens and 1.8–2.6x faster inference across 11 benchmarks.
items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents: LLM agents that think in latent space, act through text

items.summary: An item asking how you'd know what's going on without running your own LLM proxy, pointing at proxy/observability setup for LLM traffic.
items.title: If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?

items.summary: Agent Standup is a free, MIT-licensed tool that reads local session files from Claude Code, Codex, Mistral Vibe and Cowork to show agent status in a live team call and session board at zero token cost; it runs as a VS Code extension, terminal command or desktop app.
items.title: Atoll92/agent-standup

items.summary: Petal is an open-source low-latency, high-resolution screen-sharing and remote-control app where shared windows appear as movable, resizable windows with labeled cursors and instant mouse/keyboard input; it supports rooms and LiveKit, including self-hosted infrastructure.
items.title: Show HN: Petal, open-source CoScreen/ScreenHero finally free

items.summary: Free Pascal and Lazarus now have a first full release of dynamic package support, allowing components, controls and IDE extensions to be installed without rebuilding the IDE and enabling native Pascal plugin libraries with new RTL metadata and runtime handling.
items.title: Free Pascal compiler now supports dynamic packages

items.summary: Conference recap on AI monetization economics, reporting that two-thirds of Forbes AI 50 companies use usage-based pricing and that leaders are adopting hybrid subscriptions with credits and multiple outcome-based billable metrics.
items.title: The “alien” economics of AI monetization

items.summary: A free MIT-licensed CSS animation snippet library with 25+ copy-paste effects, an optional 2 KB scroll-reveal script, CSS-variable rebranding, and built-in reduced-motion and keyboard-focus accessibility.
items.title: aidenleads/css-animation-snippets

items.summary: A WebKit post explaining identity resolution, a post-cookie tracking scheme that links opaque IDs to email addresses for cross-site and cross-device profiling, alongside WebKit’s tracking-prevention policy and privacy protections.
items.title: Blocking Identity Resolution Infrastructure

items.summary: A vLLM blog post describes agent-assisted optimization of Kimi K3, including a unified CuTe DSL decode path on NVIDIA GB300 and reported 1.5–2× higher decode throughput plus a proposed fast-track RFC to reduce review burden.
items.title: Hyper Optimizing Kimi K3 in vLLM

items.summary: A book/blog series on building AI agents from first principles, growing a ~300-line toy Python agent across 16 chapters; each chapter presents a failure, a minimal harness patch, and its cost.
items.title: Harness Engineering 101: The LLM is the brain, the harness is the body

items.summary: A Google Research GitHub framework for recursive agent harnessing that keeps model weights fixed, refining task execution and a persistent improvement harness; it reports benchmark gains and supports OpenCode and Codex executors.
items.title: Harness2 by Google Research – Recursive Agent Harnessing

items.summary: Laminar's Launch HN introduces flow-1, an RL-trained model for finding errors in agent traces; it reportedly matches GPT-6-sol detection quality at 23x lower cost, making unsampled trace analysis affordable.
items.title: Launch HN: Laminar (YC S24) – RL-trained model that finds errors in agent traces

items.summary: A guide to running Claude Code and other AI coding agents in tmux: session-per-project naming, pane layouts, send-keys to script an agent, capture-pane to read it back, a status-line monitor, and the limits hit at four agents. It starts with Claude Code's built-in --worktree --tmux flags.
items.title: Tmux and Claude Code: Sessions, Send-Keys, and the Ceiling

items.summary: Scrawl, a macOS (Apple silicon, macOS 26+) and Windows preview app that records screen, voice and on-screen drawing, then bundles them into a contact sheet, keyframes, transcript timeline and manifest so a coding agent can see a problem instead of reading a description. Ships an installable agent skill and CLI.
items.title: kitlangton/scrawl

items.summary: KiviDB, a Rust multi-threaded Redis/Valkey alternative speaking RESP2/RESP3, with sharded in-memory design, snapshots plus optional AOF, and built-in FT.* full-text and vector (FLAT/HNSW) search. Claims 21M pipelined GETs/sec on 32 cores, about 9× Redis 8 and 2.3× Dragonfly.
items.title: Show HN: KiviDB, a faster Redis-compatible memory database and vector cache

items.summary: A Stripe survey of 200 platform leaders identifying four ways SaaS platforms adapt to AI: internal/product AI, usage/outcome pricing, revenue mix, and embedded finance; it notes 180% YoY growth in new platform businesses and 57% fear AI-driven customer loss.
items.title: Stripe survey: Four trends reshaping how SaaS platforms compete in the AI era

items.summary: braiNOTES is an open-source browser app for handwritten notes over lecture PDFs, with pen tools, whiteboards, offline saving, PDF/PNG export, and an optional local bridge letting a coding agent read and write pages.
items.title: Show HN: BraiNOTES, handwritten notes on your lecture PDFs in a browser tab

items.summary: A Smashing Magazine exploration of the native CSS random() function, now shipped in Safari and rolling out in Chrome 156, with CodePen demos for organic typography, bouncing letters, splayed cards, and a punk fanzine.
items.title: Embracing Playful Imperfection With The CSS `random()` Function

items.summary: axuse is an accessibility-first browser and computer-use MCP server for agent harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode). It instruments the DOM, accessibility tree and CDP instead of using a screenshot loop, has zero npm dependencies and needs Node 22+.
items.title: ctoldigital/axuse

items.summary: DeepInfer is an open-source high-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models, used in DeepSeek's production services. It offers offline inference with optimized kernels, MoE parallelism, speculative decoding, batch-invariant inference, deterministic sampling and structured outputs.
items.title: DeepInfer: High-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models

items.summary: EAGLE-4 is a speculative decoding drafter for accelerating LLM inference that adapts its strategy to batch size, hardware and workload. The eagle-harness pip package serves EAGLE-4 drafts on SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed via engine hooks.
items.title: eagle-hq/EAGLE-4

items.summary: A WhatsApp MCP server that runs in your own Cloudflare account lets an AI agent search and read your WhatsApp chats. It links once as a device, stores messages in a SQLite Durable Object and cannot send messages.
items.title: Show HN: WhatsApp MCP running free on Cloudflare

items.summary: ra-jit is a Rust JIT toolchain that applies live code edits to an already-running program in about a millisecond while preserving state, plus faster incremental builds via `cargo ra-jit build|run|test|check`. Benchmarks on ripgrep, nushell and others show builds 3–20x faster than incremental cargo.
items.title: indexable-inc/ra-jit

items.summary: tsrs is a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built by Cloudflare and VoidZero with Owner.com's Max Schwenk inside the Oxc toolchain rather than as a fork. Early benchmarks claim up to 8x speedups and ~70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, with some optimizations upstreamed.
items.title: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust

items.summary: Stackyard is a free open-source Windows/macOS app that inventories every SDK, toolchain and framework version on a machine, shows which projects use each, flags what is safe to remove, and fixes problems in one click. It also offers a marketplace of publisher-sourced SDK installs with hash verification.
items.title: AqibJavedZeepalm/stackyard

items.summary: Josh Comeau's blog post on upcoming CSS features, walking through his top 10 votes for Interop 2027, starting with the proposed @function rule for defining reusable CSS functions. Includes tips usable today.
items.title: The Future of CSS

items.summary: A FlowingData chart post on 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances data showing net worth percentiles by age group, with a table of median, 90th and 99th percentile figures per age bracket.
items.title: Rising to higher net worth, by age

items.summary: Sumi.css, a minimalist classless-first CSS framework: one 6.7 KB file, no build step, no JS or dependencies. Styles headings, forms, tables, cards, accordions, modals and nav from plain semantic HTML, with light/dark mode, custom-property theming, zero-specificity overrides and ARIA-driven states.
items.title: Show HN: Sumi.css – CSS Framework

items.summary: MyAgent is a Python general-purpose Agent Runtime repo built around a harness that handles permissions, tool execution, context compression, long-term memory, SKILL.md-based skills with self-evolution, an MCP stdio client, and sub-agents, supporting both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.
items.title: ztt0216/MyAgent

items.summary: Omnara is an open-source, self-hostable managed agent platform (Apache 2.0) positioned as an alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API, running agents on any model and machine with tools, secrets, permissions and streaming; agents are launched via agent.yaml, a Node CLI, or a TypeScript SDK.
items.title: Show HN: Omnara – Open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents

items.summary: Antirion is an open-source AI gateway shipped as a single Rust binary with a built-in admin console, routing requests across many model providers with fallback chains, cost budgets, guardrails, caching and MCP/agent gateways, claiming lower overhead and higher throughput than Bifrost and LiteLLM.
items.title: eliasbiondo/antirion

items.summary: MemT-1.0 is a family of memory foundation models (Nano and Flash) that make persistent, dynamically evolving memory part of model computation via local and hyper memory blocks with Mixture-of-Storage, cutting storage roughly 66x versus full-context KV cache at 128K history and ranking first and second on 11 memory benchmarks.
items.title: MemTensor/MemT-1.0

items.summary: Claude Super Sidebar is a plugin giving a native Claude Code pane plus a read-only local Codex session dashboard that shows main agent/subagent relationships, execution status and task steps in one panel, with no frontend build. Its docs flag that current native engine validation and latest isolation regressions remain unverified.
items.title: Zafer-Liu/claude-super-sidebar

items.summary: stalemap is an npm tool that finds dependencies whose APIs changed after a coding model's training cutoff and informs the agent via AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md notes, a type-check guard after each edit, and a search_changes MCP tool. In a pre-registered blind benchmark of 66 tasks, agents passed 89% of sessions versus 68% with no help.
items.title: Umair/stalemap

items.summary: LayerFS is a filesystem for AI coding agents where each tool call is a commit on a branch, forks are zero-cost metadata copies, same-file clashes are refused, and every line records the step that wrote it. It also keeps ignored files and claims ~0.05s mounts versus ~5 min reinstall.
items.title: LayerFS: The filesystem for AI coding agents

items.summary: A data analysis of movie shot counts from 1920 through 2025, showing a long-term increase and recent plateau, based on TransNet V2 transition detection and shot counting.
items.title: Increasing number of shots in movies

items.summary: An interactive data story on the “Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon” that calculates actor remoteness and finds Samuel L. Jackson, not Kevin Bacon, is Hollywood’s most central actor, with women underrepresented in the top 100.
items.title: The Real Kevin Bacon

items.summary: A blog article on building an isolated preview for AI-generated HTML, starting from the naive iframe srcdoc approach, breaking it three ways, then rebuilding it to show tested protections and their limits.
items.title: Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML

items.summary: OpenShell, a runtime that sandboxes fleets of autonomous AI agents, enforcing per-agent policy on file access, syscalls and network via kernel instrumentation and formally verifying policy changes before approval. 0.1.x adds a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface and new APIs.
items.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents

items.summary: A blog post arguing that asking an LLM for a confidence score or probability produces a number with no good reason to be trusted, illustrated by comparing machine confidence to a weather forecaster's, whose certainty is a calculation over information, not an opinion.
items.title: Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea

items.summary: Lampline, a local-first platform that imports Dialogflow CX and CX Agent Studio agents and runs them on your own hardware, with a drag-and-drop builder mixing LLM and scripted steps, test console, HTTP/MCP tools and phone calls via Twilio, Telnyx or SIP, at roughly $0.02–0.17 a call.
items.title: C4rohan/Lampline

items.summary: DecisionPivot (formerly DecideBench), a benchmark and code repo for evaluating decision models that output option probabilities at LLM system control points, measuring correctness, robustness to one decisive detail changing, and how much work a model handles at a fixed error rate.
items.title: StartLuxLabs/DecisionPivot

items.summary: A dbos.dev blog post on making Postgres DELETE scale, explaining MVCC delete costs and tuning cache/index performance in a Postgres-backed durable workflows and queues workload to apply retention policies at tens of thousands of workflows and steps per second.
items.title: How Postgres DELETE can actually scale

items.summary: A GitHub-hosted OpenAI CLI for calling the OpenAI REST API from a terminal or shell scripts, with commands to generate images, upload/download files, submit and wait on batches, list models, and format output as JSON/JSONL; it also distinguishes itself from Codex CLI.
items.title: OpenAI CLI

items.summary: A yoyo-code.com blog post on why 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler, covering the next-generation trait solver, the Polonius borrow checker, and compiler-performance work as long-term initiatives reach final steps.
items.title: 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler (and me)

items.summary: Chrome's experimental HTML-in-Canvas API, now in origin trial, lets developers draw DOM content into a 2D canvas or WebGL/WebGPU texture while keeping the UI interactive and accessible, avoiding the usual DOM-versus-canvas tradeoff.
items.title: The HTML-in-Canvas API origin trial

items.summary: Safari Technology Preview 255 release notes list WebKit fixes across accessibility, animations, and CSS, including corrected getComputedStyle() pseudo-element animation checks, view transition update callback flushing, and font-family: initial resolution.
items.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 255

items.summary: A blog post recounts a side project that hosted HTML files in an afternoon and, eight months later, drew as many weekly users as the company’s $150k Looker licence, with Looker usage down a third.
items.title: Can we replace a $150k Looker with a bucket of HTML files?
